title: Solving with HiGHS and reading results

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A maximizing MILP stops with termination condition maxTimeLimit and solution status feasible, incumbent 51,200 and bound 51,900. What can the nightly report say?

options.text: A plan worth 51,900 may exist; none worth 51,200 does yet
options.says: Status feasible means a plan satisfying every row is in hand; on medium the 1-node run loaded a plan of 222 starts.

options.text: A plan worth 51,200 exists; no plan can beat it
options.says: Feasible is not optimal: only the bound says how good the plan is, and here it is 700 above.

options.text: A plan worth 51,900 exists; no plan can beat it
options.says: The bound is what no plan can beat, proven by the solver; no plan worth 51,900 has been found.

options.text: A plan worth 51,200 exists; one up to 51,900 may too
options.says: Right: the incumbent is a real plan and the bound caps every plan, as with 226,745 and 226,915 on medium.

origin.section: A Limit Leaves a Feasible Plan That Is Not Proven Optimal

questions.stem: A nightly MILP now returns infeasibleOrUnbounded with no solution. Last week someone added an integer variable with no upper bound and a positive objective coefficient. Which response fits?

options.text: The variable can grow without limit; give it a maximum value
options.says: Right: the lesson's 'loan' variable gave exactly this status; the fix is a bound, not a relaxed rule.

options.text: The variable can grow without limit; relax a budget row
options.says: infeasibleOrUnbounded does not say infeasible; the lesson warns that reading it as infeasible sends a planner after a conflict that does not exist.

options.text: The variable can grow without limit; rerun the solve as is
options.says: The model is unchanged, so a rerun returns the same status; the lesson's unbounded MILP returned it on every run.

options.text: The variable can grow without limit; reload the optimal plan
options.says: The solution status was noSolution: there is no plan to load.

origin.section: An Infeasible Solve Raises Unless You Ask It to Return

questions.stem: A crew model maximizes value minus overtime cost. Overtime hours are its only continuous variable, priced $50, $65 and $90 an hour by tier, and the optimal plan buys hours in the $65 tier. The binaries are fixed at the plan, integrality is relaxed and the LP is re-solved with a dual Suffix. What price per hour does the dual of the hours-available row give?

options.text: 0, since the $65 tier's hours are fixed with the binaries
options.says: Fixing the binaries leaves the overtime hours free; the contractor model's crew row got 70, not 0.

options.text: 50, since the $65 tier is reached only after the first tier
options.says: The dual prices the last unit bought, which sits in the $65 tier; the contractor plan's dual was the third tier's 70.

options.text: 65, since the next hour would come from the $65 tier
options.says: Right: one more hour of your own saves one hour bought at the current tier, as one crew-month saved $70k in the lesson.

options.text: None, since the $65 tier makes the cost curve nonlinear
options.says: Each tier is a linear piece; after fixing and relaxing, the model is an LP and HiGHS returned duals (the crews row's 70).
